title: Printed curve y = x² − 2x − 3
subject: Mathematics

source: Seeded from mathematics/y11 lesson 69 (Printed curve y = x² − 2x − 3 (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 69: Revision: solving equations with graphs; gradients of curves. To understand how intersections of graphs solve equations and how tangents estimate gradients of curves

questions.q: Find where y = 2x meets y = x² − 3.
questions.model: Set equal: x² − 3 = 2x, so x² − 2x − 3 = 0, (x − 3)(x + 1) = 0, x = 3 or −1. y = 2x gives (3, 6) and (−1, −2).

questions.q: Which line solves x² − 3x − 5 = 0 using y = x² − 2x − 3?
Read the solutions of x² − 2x − 3 = 0 from the graph.
Core: Find the points where y = x² − 4 meets y = 3x.
Extend : The graph of y = x³ − 3x is drawn. Find the line to draw to solve x³ − 5x + 1 = 0.
Stretch : Estimate the gradient of y = x² at x = 3 using the chord from x = 2.9 to x = 3.1. Explain why it is a good estimate.
questions.a: (9.61 − 8.41) ÷ 0.2 = 6; the chord is very short and centred on x = 3, so it is close to the tangent
